newsitem.title: USA: Borg-Warner Security on track for '97 EPS rise.
newsitem.headline: Borg-Warner Security on track for '97 EPS rise.

text.p: Borg-Warner Security Corp said Monday it was on track to increase earnings per share by 30 to 45 percent in 1997.

"The year-to-date increase in income from continuing operations of 80 percent has us on course to achieve our previously stated target of 30-45 percent earnings per share growth for the year," J. Joe Adorjan, chairman, said in a statement.
Borg-Warner Security had operating earnings for 1996 of $0.59 a share.

For the first six months of the year, Borg-Warner Security had $8.1 million in income from continuing operations, up from $4.5 million a year ago. For the second quarter, income from continuing operations rose to $4.1 million from $2.9 million.
Revenues for the second quarter fell to $378.6 million from $418.3 million. Core security services revenues in the quarter were $378.6 million, up from $357.6 million.

The decline in overall revenues was due to the January 1997 combination of its Wells Fargo Armored business with Loomis Armored division. Loomis, Fargo & Co is 49 percent owned by Borg-Warner Security and 51 percent by Loomis shareholders.
